title: quant-sweep-execution-handoff-retention-roles
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Create a robust orchestration layer in the Console for quantization sweep runs that covers execution handoff between scheduler and worker fleets, artifact lifecycle (storage, immutability, TTL/GC), and fine-grained role-based access to run metadata and artifacts. This ticket scopes UI flows, API contracts, retention/default TTLs, and RBAC mappings required to safely store FP8/INT8 calibration outputs and enable accuracy validation and replayability while minimizing storage costs and surface area for sensitive data.
background: Teams are running calibration sweeps that produce multiple artifacts: calibration traces, per-layer scale/fp stats, candidate quant profiles, and validation evals. Today artifacts live in ad-hoc storage buckets and access is inconsistent. We need a unified orchestration + storage policy so runs are discoverable, reproducible, cost-controlled, and auditable for enterprise customers (Private/Dedicated).
acceptance_criteria: Console exposes a Sweep Run page that shows run state, start/end timestamps, produced artifacts list with size and hash, and a link to a validation report.

API endpoints: POST /runs to start a sweep, GET /runs/:id to retrieve run metadata, POST /runs/:id/retry to re-run failed stages, and GET /runs/:id/artifacts to list and stream artifacts. Endpoints return stable artifact URLs with short-lived signed access tokens.

Retention policies: default TTL for calibration artifacts is 90 days, configurable per-organization; artifacts older than TTL are soft-deleted (tombstone) and eligible for GC after an additional 30 days. Console shows TTL and graveyard status and supports manual restore during tombstone window.

RBAC: roles map to actions: 'ml-engineer' can start/rerun and download artifacts; 'platform-admin' can modify TTLs and purge artifacts; 'auditor' can view metadata and audit logs but cannot download payloads. RBAC enforced at API layer and logged to audit trail.

Artifact immutability and signing: completed runs create read-only artifact manifests with SHA256 digests; manifest signing ensures integrity; modifying a run artifact requires an explicit 'recreate run' operation which creates a new run id.

Validation gating: console flags runs where validation metrics (WER/accuracy/perplexity) deviate from baseline beyond configured thresholds; these flags are surfaced in run summary and can optionally block auto-promotion to serving model variants.

Operational metrics: job queue length, average time in scheduling, worker failure rate, artifact ingress bytes/day, and TTL-expiry GC counts are emitted to observability and appear in Console's Calibration Ops dashboard.
Docs and SDK: JS/Python SDK wrappers for starting/scrubbing/listing runs available with examples for replays and for fetching signed URLs.
tasks: PM: finalize UX copy for run lifecycle, tombstone UX, and permission matrix
Design: mock Sweep Run page, artifact list, TTL editor modal, and RBAC settings panel
Eng (API): implement stable run API endpoints, signed artifact URL generation, and RBAC checks
Eng (Scheduler): implement handoff protocol for queued sweeps -> worker fleets, ensure idempotent retries
Eng (Storage): implement artifact manifest format, immutability enforcement, TTL/tombstone lifecycle and GC job
Eng (Auth): map roles to permissions, integrate with existing RBAC and audit logging, add delegated run tokens for external CI
QA: end-to-end test: start run -> produce artifacts -> simulate TTL expiration -> restore from tombstone
Docs: runbook for ops teams describing cost implications and manual purge steps
Security: threat review for signed URLs and artifact encryption at rest (KMS note)
notes: Use manifest format: run_id, artifact_name, sha256, size_bytes, storage_path, created_at, signed_by
Signed URLs should be short lived (default 15 minutes) and require 'artifact:read' scope; longer scopes allowed for org-admins via Console
Consider two storage classes: hot (30 days) and cold (remaining TTL) to reduce cost for long-tail artifacts
Support partial reruns that reuse cached prefix/KV traces to speed calibration sweep replay
For Private deployments, artifacts should be optionally enforceable to remain in-customer S3/VPC endpoints; add storage backend abstraction
